title: Refund at the boundary — 39 seats, the last count that still refunds
poolIdNote: Deliberately unnamed, as T5 was. The plan is written to run against whichever pool is open when this freeze merges, so nothing about the pool can have shaped the prediction. The freeze record names the pool once the first entry lands.
hypothesis: The fork between refunding and playing is at exactly 40 seats, and 39 is on the refunding side of it. A pool holding 39 entries at its fill deadline cannot seal: seal_at_deadline reverts with FieldBelowMinimum and trigger_refund flips the pool to Refunding, returns the untouched 4 SOL pot from the prize vault to the platform treasury, and refund pays each of the 39 entrants their full entry price back out of the treasury. No ranking, no scoring, no prize and no reviewer is involved. T1 proved this at 12 seats, far from the boundary; T2 proves it one seat below the boundary, which is where an off-by-one in the comparison would hide.

expectations.settlementIsPermissionless: Both trigger_refund and refund are permissionless (refund.rs): any signer may settle a pool that missed its deadline below MIN_SEATS, so a vanished operator cannot strand entries. This test therefore needs no admin key and no founder action after the entries land.
expectations.vaultAfterNote: the rent cushion, never recovered — this is not zero, and a zero here would be the surprise
expectations.perSeatSunkNote: THIS NUMBER IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED, WHICH MAKES IT A SHARPER PREDICTION THAN T1'S. T1's plan carried 4436000 from docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md. Three settled pools have since measured the same figure to the lamport: T1 (pool 14, refunded) 4441080; T4 (pool 16, scored) 4441080; T5 (pool 18, scored) 4441080. The estimate was 0.11% low. T2 predicts 4441080 EXACTLY for every one of the 39 seats — a single lamport of drift on any seat is a failure, not rounding.
expectations.routeMakesNoDifference: Both founder wallets are refunded on identical terms to the 37 headless ones — same refund, same sunk cost, to the lamport. The refund path reads an Entry, not a route.

seatNote: Seat indices are assigned by the chain in arrival order and are recorded at harvest. Battle sets are NOT predicted here, for the same reason T1's were not: a refund pool is never scored, and no rank or payout depends on any allocation. This is what lets a refund plan be frozen without an oracle. The allocations are still sealed and their hashes still committed on chain, so the sealing property is exercised exactly as it is on a scored pool — what is missing is only the reveal.
contingency: STOPPING SHORT IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE CLAIM, AND THE PLAN IS NOT EDITED IF IT HAPPENS. Any seat that does not land reconciles as ABSENT. Every count below 40 takes the identical fork, so a pool that finishes at 37 or 38 still proves the refund property — it just stops proving the BOUNDARY, which is T2's specific reason for existing. Should the run stop short, the reduced count is recorded as a deviation and the boundary claim is retried on a later pool rather than restated at a lower number. Landing 41 would be worse than landing 37: it would cross the fork and turn this into T3.
passCriteria: The pool reaches Closed, not Paid.
It holds exactly 39 entrants at its fill deadline — one below the minimum field.
trigger_refund settles it; seal_at_deadline is not what closes this pool.
Every entrant's balance rises by exactly 100000000 lamports at refund.
Each entrant's net loss over the whole test is exactly 4441080 lamports — the figure three settled pools have already measured, predicted here to the lamport.
Both founder wallets are refunded on identical terms to the 37 headless seats.
The prize vault ends holding exactly 650240 lamports.
The pot of 4000000000 lamports returns to the platform treasury untouched.
No seat is flagged, no sanctions hold is placed, and no reviewer is involved.
